source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2405.07026v4, 22 May 2026; journal version cited by the core was not directly inspectable
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a computable selectively valid randomization distribution under its adaptive-design assumptions, explicitly identifies choice of holdout quantity/stage and powerful selection-dependent statistics as open practical questions, and illustrates adaptive weighting only numerically.

Theorem 1 represents sequential policies by trajectory variables and the paper relaxes the resulting binary program to a sparse LP for discretized, model-based adaptive-enrichment policy optimization under power and familywise-error constraints.

The article proves a selective central-limit transfer under independent sampling and randomized response selection; it does not state a finite-population without-replacement selected-reference transfer.

The paper develops general finite-population CLTs for randomization-based causal analysis, including randomization tests and repeated-sampling distributions, but the stated description is unconditional rather than enrichment-cell conditional.

The paper derives Berry--Esseen bounds for linear permutational statistics under completely randomized experiments and develops variance-estimation results; it does not supply the proposed selected-cell ratio/reference-quantile transfer.

The paper studies optimal conditional inference in batched parametric Gaussian bandit experiments, characterizing last-batch optimality and additional location-invariant leftover information; this is not the fixed-potential-outcomes rank-statistic design problem proposed here.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Rewrite uniform-selected-transfer with two explicitly indexed laws: an alternative finite-population sampling array satisfying local alternatives and a sharp-null imputed reference array used only to define the conditional randomization law.
Replace the selected-quantile equality clause with a stated equality condition in terms of c1,c2,t and q_beta(r,·), then prove its correspondence to any Ehrhard--Borell equality case used.
Add Zhang and Gao's 2025 Adaptive Sample Splitting for Randomization Tests to related work and state precisely why its split construction does not cover the full-cell rank-weight frontier.

recommended_next_step: Revise the incompatible null/alternative premise structure and formalize the selected-quantile equality clause, then return this field-tier novelty kernel to review.
